rapport_notes: Patient and reassuring with a demanding, detail-oriented customer who was anxious about a genuinely tricky furniture-fit problem (a 6-foot desk through a 5-foot hallway); stayed professional through some repetitive back-and-forth about email vs. text.
process_discipline_notes: No repeats or violations from the rep.

evidence_quotes.agenda: not asked as a formal line — the customer launched straight into her own concern (the desk/hallway fit) before any agenda question was posed.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep engaged the fit concern over multiple turns: asked for a photo, asked about hallway dimensions, explained the neighbor's-door workaround, and asked for an itemized list — genuine multi-turn digging, not a single question and pivot.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: not covered — no pricing was ever given on this call

top_strength: Stayed calm, patient, and solution-oriented with a customer who was visibly anxious about a genuinely tricky furniture-fit problem, correctly recognizing that photos and precise measurements were needed before quoting rather than guessing and risking a bad on-site surprise.
coaching_note: None of the core differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, communication) were mentioned at all — even though pricing was deferred, these trust-building lines could have been worked in while waiting on the spreadsheet and likely would have eased the customer's visible anxiety about her fragile, heavy items.
